ECE 6390 / RF links

Link budget

From the figure to the physics

Fig. 1 shows how carrier power, noise density and bit rate connect in one link budget.

With consistent logarithmic references, received carrier power is C = EIRP − LFS − Lother + Gr. Each term belongs to a specified physical plane, and each included loss is applied once.

Input-referred noise density is N₀ = kBTsys in W/Hz. Subtracting its dBW/Hz value from carrier power in dBW gives C/N₀ in dB-Hz.

For bit rate Rb in bit/s, Eb/N₀ in dB equals C/N₀ − 10 log₁₀Rb. This metric separates energy per bit from the receiver's chosen noise bandwidth; a modulation and coding model is still needed to predict error rate.

Example

EIRP = 40 dBW, LFS = 200 dB, other losses = 2 dB, and Gr = 30 dBi give C = −132 dBW. Separately, C/N₀ = 70 dB-Hz at 1 Mbit/s gives Eb/N₀ = 10 dB.

Model and course sources

    Practice

    1. If carrier power and noise density remain fixed while bit rate doubles, what happens to Eb/N₀?

    Only the 10 log₁₀Rb term changes.

    Eb/N₀ falls by 10 log₁₀2 ≈ 3.01 dB because the same received power is spread across twice as many bits per second.
